To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a static analysis is presented for tracking implicit information flow and quantitative information leakage of mobile applications; (ii) the presented analysis is implemented as part of the tool AppSage; and (iii) the analysis of a set of 20 Android applications shows that implicit flows are present in a significant number of them, and that the quantitative analysis is useful for identifying applications that leak more information than others.

we have developed a novel approach for analyzing information flows in Android applications, and that we have shown that it can detect a large number of privacy violations in real-world Android applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we automatically analyze the information flow of mobile apps?
the following questions: (i) How can we model the information flow in a mobile application?

the following aspects: (i) a static analysis for verifying compliance with privacy policies of mobile applications, based on the concept of abstract interpretation; (ii) an analysis that properly extends previous work by tracking implicit information flows; and (iii) a quantitative analysis that computes the amount of information leaked in the application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Android applications have a high potential for privacy leakage.
Android is not a secure platform and it is not possible to develop secure apps on it.
the privacy analysis of Android applications is a very important and useful tool, which should be further developed and used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a static analysis for verifying compliance of mobile applications to privacy policies.
we have developed a static analysis for Android apps that is capable of detecting both the explicit and implicit information flows.
we have proposed a static analysis for verifying privacy policy of mobile applications by combining the data centric semantics with the quantitative analysis of information flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the qualitative analysis is necessary for detecting privacy leaks, the quantitative analysis is necessary for assessing the severity of the leaks and for ranking the applications.
a combination of qualitative and quan- titative analyses is required for an adequate verification of privacy policy com- pliance.
, while the qualitative information flow analysis can be used to detect potential privacy violations, the quantitative analysis is necessary to understand the severity of the privacy leak.
